summary: A short addendum to RFC 987, which maps between X.400 and RFC 822 mail. It was a proposed protocol and asked for discussion. It updates RFC 987 and was updated by RFC 1138 and RFC 1148, and replaced by RFC 1327 and RFC 2156.

plainLanguage.summary: This addendum corrects and extends the mapping rules between X.400 and RFC 822 addresses. It clarifies component order and introduces a marker for an omitted component.

subtitle: Adds ordering rules and omitted-component support to the X.400 and RFC 822 mapping.

tldr.problem: RFC 987's X.400 and RFC 822 mapping needed corrections, clearer ordering for repeated name components, and a way to represent omitted components.
tldr.mechanism: This addendum fixes errata, defines component ordering, uses @ to mark an omitted value, and adds table syntax for mapping in both directions.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1026 was updated by RFCs 1138 and 1148 and obsoleted by RFCs 1327 and 2156.

facts.label: Allowed table components
facts.value: C, ADMD, PRMD, O and OU

today: RFC 1026 was updated by RFC 1138 and RFC 1148, and obsoleted by RFC 1327 and RFC 2156.

sections.title: Corrections to RFC 987
sections.content:
RFC 1026 lists additions and corrections to RFC 987, also called Mailgroup Note 19. It says the addendum carries equal weight to the original specification for the stated mapping communities.

The errata include replacing a doubled period with a single period, correcting section references and changing several grammar forms to use the 1# notation.
sections.plainLanguage: The addendum fixes typographical and syntax-reference errors in RFC 987. It says its corrections carry the same weight as the original.

sections.title: Ordering Name Components
sections.content:
Most O/R name component ordering is not significant for the mapping. Organisational Units and Domain Defined Attributes, however, are sequences in P1.ORName, so the mapping needs consistent order and must preserve it across mappings.

For both component types, the first item in the sequence is most significant. In the text encoding used in the local part of an RFC 822 address, the most significant component appears on the right. The RFC says these rules do not imply ordering significance within X.400 itself.
sections.plainLanguage: The rules specify which repeated name component is most significant. They also define where that component appears in the text form.

sections.title: Omitted Components and Mapping Tables
sections.content:
The addendum addresses naming cases where Organisation or PRMD is omitted. It introduces an explicit missing component: the value @ in the extended dmn-orname syntax represents an omitted attribute, separately from an attribute with a null value.

A new Appendix F defines separate table formats for domain-to-X.400 and X.400-to-domain mapping because the mapping is not symmetric. It restricts the component types and says to use the longest possible match when several matches apply.
sections.plainLanguage: The @ marker says a name component is intentionally omitted. Appendix F defines separate lookup-table forms for each mapping direction.

references.text: Kille, S., "Mapping between X.400 and RFC 822", RFC 987.
